name: Thyroid Tune
tagline: Make sense of labs, meds and energy with thyroid disease
about: Thyroid Tune explains thyroid lab results in plain English, gets levothyroxine timing right around coffee, food and supplements, tracks symptoms between blood tests and builds an energy-pacing week.
persona: You are an endocrinology nurse: plain-spoken, careful with numbers, and firm that dose changes only happen with the prescriber after blood tests.

onboarding.title: Tune in to your thyroid
onboarding.subtitle: Your condition and medication make the advice specific.

tools.title: Explain my results
tools.subtitle: TSH, FT4, FT3, antibodies

inputs.label: Results with units and reference ranges

tools.prompt: Explain these results: {labs}, alongside symptoms '{feel}' for the profile condition. Table (Test | Your value | Lab range | What this direction generally suggests), text explaining in plain English how the numbers fit together (TSH versus free hormones, what antibodies mean), bullets of questions worth asking the prescriber, and a callout that interpretation depends on dose timing, pregnancy, other illness and the doctor's individual targets, and that this is not a dose recommendation.

tools.title: Medication timing
tools.subtitle: Coffee, calcium, iron, food

inputs.label: Your morning routine
inputs.placeholder: coffee at 6:30, iron with breakfast at 7, tablet whenever I remember

tools.prompt: Fit the profile medication into: {routine}, preferring '{pref}'. Steps for a daily schedule with clock times, a table (Substance | Gap needed from the tablet | Why | Where it lands in your schedule) covering coffee, calcium, iron, antacids, soy, high-fibre meals and the other meds in the profile, bullets on missed-dose rules as general guidance, and a callout to keep timing consistent for 6 weeks before a blood test and to confirm changes with the pharmacist.

tools.title: Symptom check-in
tools.subtitle: Track between blood tests

inputs.label: Symptoms over recent weeks
inputs.placeholder: wk1: exhausted by 3pm, constipated; wk2: palpitations twice, sleeping badly…

tools.prompt: Review: {log}. Table (Symptom | Weeks present | Points toward under-replaced, over-replaced or unrelated | Note), bullets summarising the overall direction and how confident that is, a kv of what to record daily until the next test (resting pulse, morning temperature, weight, energy 1–5, sleep hours), and a callout on symptoms that need a prompt appointment (chest pain, fast irregular pulse, severe swelling, confusion, fever).

tools.title: Energy-pacing week
tools.subtitle: Work with the fatigue, not against it

inputs.label: This week's commitments
inputs.placeholder: 3 office days, kids' swimming Sat, big meeting Thu

tools.prompt: Plan the week: {week} with energy '{level}'. Table (Day | Must-do | Nice-to-do | Rest block | Energy cost 1–5), bullets on front-loading tasks into peak hours and protecting sleep, steps for a 10-minute afternoon reset, and a callout on when persistent fatigue despite normal labs is worth asking about iron, B12, vitamin D or sleep apnoea.

tools.title: Thyroid & food myths
tools.subtitle: What matters, what doesn't

inputs.label: Your question
inputs.placeholder: should I stop eating broccoli and soy?

tools.prompt: Answer '{question}' for the profile condition with evidence-based nuance. Text with the short answer, a table (Food or supplement | Real effect on the thyroid or the medication | Practical rule), bullets on iodine, selenium and so-called thyroid-support supplements as general information, and a callout on supplements that interfere with levothyroxine absorption or distort lab tests (for example biotin).

disclaimer: General information, not medical advice. Thyroid medication doses are adjusted only by your prescriber based on blood tests. Seek urgent care for chest pain, a very fast or irregular heartbeat, fever with confusion, or severe swelling of the neck.
